text.p: Genentech Inc and IDEC Pharmaceuticals Corp said they applied for Food and Drug Administration approval of the IDEC-C2B8, or rituximab monoclonal antibody they jointly developed for the treatment of non-Hodgkin's lymphona.
In addition, Roche Holdings's Hoffman-La Roche division has made a marketing authorization application with the European Medicines Evaluation Agency to market the treatment in Europe.
A Genentech spokeswoman said the company was hopeful the FDA would review its application on an expedited review.

If approved, IDEC-C2B8 would be the first therapeutic monoclonal antibody available in the U.S. for the treatment of cancer. Unlike conventional chemotherapy treatment, which attacks healthy as well as cancerous cells, IDEC-C2B8 is designed to specifically target the cancerous B cells, or immune system cells that proliferate in non-Hodgkin's lymphoma patients.

In Phase III clinical trials, 50 percent of patients tested showed tumor shrinkage of 50 percent or greater after four weekly infusions with the drug. Of those patients who responded, 70 percent were still in remission at a median follow-up time of over nine months.

Genentech, which is applying the monoclonal antibody approach to develop treatment for other cancers as well, currently has another antibody, HER2, in Phase III clinical trials as a treatment for breast cancer.
